title: Lightime
subtitle: A desktop zoned lighting table lamp using FOC and depth detection

mainContent.content: A desktop lamp using FOC motor control and depth sensing to create zoned lighting on a table. Different tasks get different pools of light without complex UI — the desk understands where you are working and steers light accordingly.

content.title: 3D render of the Lightime desk lamp with wooden base and articulated arm

mainContent.content: The pendulum-inspired form balances aesthetics and function. The wooden base houses the FOC motor while the articulated arm enables precise beam steering.

content.title: Concept poster showing zoned lighting, skeletal tracking, FOC motor, and emotional feedback

mainContent.content: The poster communicates the full design vision: FOC-controlled lighting zones, hand tracking, and a pet-like mechanical response that gives the lamp personality.

content.title: System diagram showing skeletal tracking, zoned lighting, FOC motor, and emotional feedback loop

mainContent.content: The system maps the tabletop into lighting zones based on hand position. FOC motor steers the light beam while emotional feedback adds a responsive, alive quality.

content.title: Lightime prototype on exhibition table alongside traditional desk lamp for comparison

mainContent.content: Side-by-side comparison with a conventional lamp. The physical prototype demonstrates the pendulum structure and real-time light steering in an exhibition context.

content.title: Visualization of the zoned lighting system and user interaction

mainContent.content: Passive supervision combined with active user interaction. The lamp follows hand gestures unconsciously, creating a natural, gesture-driven lighting experience.

content.title: Depth detection sensor module mounted on the lamp arm

mainContent.content: The depth sensor is integrated into the lamp arm housing, enabling real-time 3D hand tracking without external cameras or markers.
